sourcedFrom: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 (2018 (typesetting stamp 3/5/18; no copyright line is printed anywhere in this book))
cleanIntro: Mossberg's own pump strip: prove it empty in three places, get the barrel off, drop the trigger housing out on its single pin, then the cartridge stop, bolt slide, bolt and elevator out of the receiver. It ends there by the maker's instruction — the trigger housing is not opened, and nothing deeper is published.

steps.title: Safety fully rearward, then prove it empty in three places
steps.action: Push the safety button on top of the receiver all the way back to ON, then check the chamber, the elevator and the magazine tube — look at each and put a finger in. Mossberg names three places rather than one because a pump can hold a shell in the tube with a clear chamber, and the tube is the one people skip.
steps.quote: Move the safety button fully rearward to the “ON” (SAFE) position and visually and physically check the chamber, elevator, and magazine tube to be certain the shotgun is unloaded before disassembling the firearm.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — DISASSEMBLY, p.11

steps.title: Eye protection on before anything under spring load moves
steps.action: Put glasses on before you start. This is not boilerplate here: the magazine spring runs the length of the tube under compression, and on the 590 and 835 the retainer that holds it is the very thing you are about to unscrew past.
steps.quote: Wear eye protection during disassembly and cleaning to protect your eyes from oil splatter or spring loaded components.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — DISASSEMBLY, p.11

steps.title: Action open, then the forearm eased forward to mid-port
steps.action: Press the action lock lever and run the forearm all the way back to open the action, then bring it slowly forward until the front of the bolt sits in the middle of the ejection port. That mid-port position is what lines the bolt slide up with the clearance cuts later — go fully forward and you will be fighting it.
steps.aside: Depress the action lock lever and open the action by sliding the forearm fully rearward.
steps.quote: Move the forearm slowly forward from the fully rearward position until the front of the bolt is in the middle of the ejection port.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — DISASSEMBLY, p.11

steps.title: Takedown screw out — counterclockwise until it clears the tube
steps.action: Turn the takedown screw at the front of the magazine tube counterclockwise and keep going until the threads are completely clear of the end of the tube. Backing it off part way is the usual mistake: the barrel will feel loose and still be captive, and levering on it then is what bends a takedown mount.
steps.quote: Loosen the takedown screw by turning it counterclockwise until the screw threads are completely disengaged from the end of the magazine tube
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — DISASSEMBLY, p.11

steps.title: Barrel off with a rocking pull, not a straight yank
steps.action: Work the barrel out of the receiver with a gentle back-and-forth rotation while you pull. The barrel extension sits in a cut in the top of the receiver and a straight pull binds it; a small twist breaks it free without scoring either part.
steps.quote: Remove the barrel from the receiver with a gentle back-and-forth rotational movement while pulling the barrel out of the receiver assembly.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — DISASSEMBLY — barrel removal, p.12

steps.title: Trigger housing pin out with a punch no bigger than 3/16”
steps.action: Lay the gun down with the trigger guard up and drift out the small trigger housing retainer pin in the side of the receiver, about a half inch below the rear of the trigger guard. Mossberg sets a maximum punch diameter of 3/16 inch — a larger punch does not fit the hole and will swell the receiver around it.
steps.quote: With a punch (no greater than 3/16” [4.76 mm] diameter), push out the small diameter trigger housing retainer pin located on the side of the receiver, approximately a 1/2” (12.7 mm) below the rear of the trigger guard
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — DISASSEMBLY — Trigger Housing Assembly Removal, p.12

steps.title: Trigger housing out rear-first — and it does not come apart
steps.action: Lift the rear of the trigger housing first and take the assembly out; the front sits on lugs that want to stay put while the back rises. Do not pull the trigger with the housing out of the receiver, and do not go inside it — Mossberg puts the internals of this assembly behind a service centre or a gunsmith.
steps.aside: The trigger housing assembly is a complex assembly and must not be disassembled.
steps.quote: Remove the trigger housing assembly by lifting the rear portion upward first.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — DISASSEMBLY — Trigger Housing Assembly Removal, p.12

steps.title: Cartridge interrupter and cartridge stop out of the receiver walls
steps.action: Take the cartridge interrupter and the cartridge stop out of the receiver. They are sprung against the inside walls and often need a light tap on the outside of the receiver to drop free. Note which side each came from before it leaves your hand — they are not interchangeable and they go back hooks-inward.
steps.aside: It may be necessary to tap the sides of the receiver lightly to release these parts
steps.quote: Remove the cartridge interrupter and cartridge stop from the receiver.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS, p.13

steps.title: Bolt slide lifted out at the clearance cuts
steps.action: Draw the forearm back until the bolt and bolt slide are about three quarters rearward, then lift the bolt slide straight up and out — it only clears when its bottom lines up with the cuts in the receiver sides. Watch how the bolt, bolt slide and slide bars sit together, because they have to go back in that same relationship.
steps.aside: Pay special attention to the position of the bolt, bolt slide and action slide bar assembly during this portion of the disassembly, as the parts must be in the same relationship during reassembly.
steps.quote: When the bottom of the bolt slide is aligned with the clearance cuts in the sides of the receiver, lift the bolt slide upward and out of the receiver
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS, p.13

steps.title: Bolt out the front, through the barrel opening
steps.action: Slide the bolt assembly forward and out through the barrel opening at the front of the receiver. It leaves the way the barrel went, not up through the ejection port — trying to lift it out of the port is how the ejector gets bent.
steps.quote: Remove the bolt assembly by sliding it forward and out of the receiver assembly through the barrel opening at the front of the receiver
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS, p.14

steps.title: Elevator out — safety still ON, then squeeze the arms
steps.action: Check the safety is still fully rearward: Mossberg makes that a condition of getting the elevator out, not a general reminder. Pivot the front of the elevator up out of the receiver, then squeeze its two open arms together until the studs clear their holes and lift it away.
steps.aside: The safety button must be fully rearward in the “ON” (SAFE) position to remove the elevator assembly.
steps.quote: Squeeze the two arms which form the open end of the elevator assembly together sufficiently to disengage and remove the elevator from the receiver
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS, p.14

steps.title: Forearm and action slide off the magazine tube — field strip complete
steps.action: Slide the forearm and action slide assembly forward off the magazine tube and the field strip is done. Mossberg stops here in as many words: this is as far as the gun comes apart for cleaning, and anything deeper is a service centre or a gunsmith, not a kitchen table.
steps.aside: Field disassembly is now complete! The shotgun should not be disassembled further for routine cleaning or maintenance.
steps.quote: Remove the forearm/action slide assembly by sliding it forward and off the magazine tube.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS, p.14

deepAbsentReason: Mossberg publishes exactly one teardown for these guns and it ends where the steps above end — barrel, trigger housing, cartridge stop and interrupter, bolt slide, bolt, elevator, forearm. The book then closes the door in its own words: "Field disassembly is now complete!" followed by "Further disassembly should only be performed by an Authorized Product Service Center or by a qualified gunsmith." There is no deeper published procedure to author, and the absence is recorded rather than filled.

cleaning.name: BARREL & CHAMBER
tasks: Scrub the bore and chamber with solvent, then patch until the patches come out clean
Finish with a lightly oiled patch for a protective film
A brass bristle brush for stubborn deposits — never leave a patch in the bore

cleaning.name: ACTION
tasks: Clean the bolt, bolt slide and action slide bars of accumulated residue
Lubricate sparingly — action parts stay clean longer dry than oily

cleaning.name: RECEIVER
tasks: Wipe the inside with a rag or soft brush, working the tracks that guide the bolt and bolt slide
A few drops of light oil in those tracks once clean
Never a metal-bristle brush — it takes the finish off

cleaning.name: TRIGGER HOUSING
tasks: Brush loose residue off with a soft bristle brush only
Do not disassemble it and do not pull the trigger while it is out of the receiver

reassembly: Receiver trigger-guard opening upward, safety still fully rearward in the ON position.
Slide the forearm assembly onto the magazine tube, guiding the action slide bars into their cuts in the front of the receiver.
Squeeze the elevator arms together and seat its studs in the 1/4 inch holes in the receiver, then pivot it level with the edge of the receiver cavity.
Enter the bolt through the barrel opening with the bolt lock down and forward, and depress the ejector so the bolt can run fully rearward — the ejector must land in its slot in the bolt.
Line the notch in the action slide bars up with the cuts in the receiver walls, push the elevator down onto the bolt, and fit the bolt slide front-first, slotted side up with the notch to the rear.
Set the cartridge stop and cartridge interrupter back on their own walls with the hooks facing inward, and hold them there with one hand.
With the hammer fully cocked, enter the trigger housing lugs into the front slots and ease the rear down — do not force it — then push the trigger housing pin in flush with the receiver.
Slide the barrel into the receiver and tighten the takedown screw finger tight only — no pliers, no wrench. A little space between the magazine tube and the takedown mount is normal.
Look through the ejection port and confirm the barrel extension is resting firmly against its cut in the top of the receiver before the gun is used.
fncheck: With the gun confirmed empty and the muzzle safe, hold the action lock lever down and work the action open and closed several times to feel it run free. Then close the action with the safety ON and pull the trigger — the hammer must not fall. Take your finger off, move the safety to OFF — the hammer must still not fall. Only then, with the safety OFF, should pulling the trigger drop the hammer. If it behaves any other way, stop and get it to a service centre rather than shooting it.
